answer: Reputation-weighted task auction. Each agent's bid weight equals its proven track record, and new identities start at zero, so a clone must earn history through real work before competing for high-value tasks. To harbor trust, the system caps first-time identities at low-stakes jobs. A sudden plume of fresh accounts bidding in unison triggers a cooldown gale that freezes their bids until the anomaly clears. Cost: each clone needs weeks of genuine completed work per identity, making mass cloning expensive in time.
